subject: MSA + Order Form — term mechanics and offramp exceptions
messages:
From: Anna Zhao <anna@quantix.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RFP: MSA + Order Form — Term & Renewal Clarifications

Hi Connor / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. As Quantix gets ready for procurement review, our legal team asked for a couple specific clarifications on term mechanics in the draft MSA and Order Form:

- Auto-renew: current MSA language auto-renews for successive 12-month periods unless either party gives notice. Can Redwood confirm whether Quantix can elect a single 12-month renewal only (i.e., auto-renew once), or whether unlimited auto-renew is required?
- Notice window: we'd prefer a 60-day non-renewal notice for pilots < $100k TCV. Is Redwood willing to accept a shorter pilot notice?
- Termination for convenience (TFC): we need clarity on Redwood's obligations on TFC — specifically transition support window and any associated credits. Quantix would like TFC to trigger a pro-rata service credit and a 90-day transition assistance.
- Staged offboarding: can Redwood accept split notice (e.g., 60 days for core infra, 120 days for archived data/transfer)?

I've attached Quantix_Security_Q_A.xlsx for completeness (not related to the term questions). Our procurement timeline is tight — appreciative if we can align on redlines this week.

Thanks,
Anna Zhao
Procurement Lead
Quantix.ai

Attachments: Quantix_Security_Q_A.xlsx

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Anna Zhao <anna@quantix.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: MSA + Order Form — Term & Renewal Clarifications

Anna — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and next steps below: 

- Auto-renew: Redwood's standard is rolling 12-month auto-renew unless countered in the Order Form. We can accommodate "auto-renew once" for pilot deals under $100k, subject to billing/commit alignment.
- Notice window: standard notice is 90 days; for pilot-sized commitments we will consider 60 days for the first renewal only.
- TFC: our standard TFC includes up to 180 days of support for data transfer and a pro-rata credit for unused committed capacity. We can tighten the transition support to 90 days if Quantix accepts a capped service-credit formula (we'll propose language).
- Staged offboarding: we can draft staggered handover mechanics (core infra cutoff vs archived data transfer) but we typically require clear dates and a handoff plan in the Order Form.

I've asked Marissa (Contracts) and Ben (Sales ops) to weigh in on drafting a short redline that captures a pilot-friendly path. If you can confirm the pilot TCV and target go-live, we'll produce a redline with two options (conservative/accelerated).

Next steps: Marissa to send a redline, Ben to confirm procurement checklist items, and I'll book a 30-min call if Quantix legal wants to walk through.

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Anna Zhao <anna@quantix.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: MSA + Order Form — Term & Renewal Clarifications

Anna / Connor — attaching an initial redline focusing only on term + termination mechanics to keep scope tight. High-level proposal: 

1) Auto-renew: Order Form option A (standard): rolling 12-month auto-renew.
   Option B (pilot-friendly): auto-renew one time for an additional 12 months; thereafter the agreement terminates unless mutually agreed in writing.
2) Notice: 60-day written notice for non-renewal for the first renewal only (pilot). Subsequent renewals revert to 90 days.
3) Termination for Convenience (TFC): Quantix may terminate for convenience with 30 days' written notice; Redwood will provide (a) pro-rata credit for pre-paid/committed fees covering remainder of terminated period, and (b) 90 days of transition assistance limited to reasonable efforts and documented handoff tasks.
4) Staged offboarding: included as an Order Form schedule (Schedule X) with defined deliverables and milestone dates; split notice allowed where each scope item is assigned a separate notice window.

I've kept the legalese minimal in this draft so Quantix can see practical options.

Attached: Redwood_MSA_term_redline_v1.docx (term redline). Happy to jump on a call; Connor please confirm if Ben should be included on the vendor side checklist.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Contracts Counsel | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Tomás Ruiz <tomas.ruiz@quantix.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Zhao <anna@quantix.ai>, legal@quantix.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: MSA + Order Form — Term & Renewal Clarifications

Marissa / Connor — thanks for the quick turnaround and concrete options. Quantix legal prefers Option B (auto-renew once) and accepts a 60-day notice for the first renewal. A few follow-ups before we can greenlight: 

- TFC: the team requests that any pro-rata credit be unambiguous (credit = remaining days / days in billing period * prepaid fees), and that transition assistance be guaranteed for 90 days with stated SLAs for data export (throughput and max latency). Can Redwood accept the credit formula?
- Split notice: good to have Schedule X. Please include an example schedule for staged offboarding (core compute cutoff, live traffic handover, and archival transfer).
- Billing holdback: procurement asks for a 30-day billing holdback on final invoice while migration verification completes. Is that acceptable?

If you can send a redline reflecting the above (credit formula + example Schedule X + note on billing holdback), we can escalate internally and aim for signature by end of month.

Cheers,
Tomás Ruiz
Head of Legal Operations
Quantix.ai
